knowledge.title: AI-operator self-correction: verify an API exists in the INSTALLED project before using it — hallucinated APIs are a recurrent, high-severity agent failure mode
knowledge.solutionUnderTest:
Before using any non-trivial API, verify it against the INSTALLED project, in this order: 1) DEPENDENCY: the package is in package.json AND the lockfile (package-lock.json / pnpm-lock.yaml / bun.lockb) — the lockfile records the exact RESOLVED version; docs describe the latest release, which may be newer. 2) INSTALLED VERSION: read node_modules/<pkg>/package.json version — the registry copy and the installed copy can differ; the installed one is what runs. 3) SYMBOL AND SIGNATURE at that version: check the package's entry .d.ts / exports map for the exact symbol — not just the name: parameter shapes and option keys drift across versions. A type check (tsc --noEmit, or the editor language server) is STRONGER than grep because it validates call shape, not just presence. 4) RUNTIME feature detection when behavior is version-dependent: guard with typeof obj.method === 'function' before relying on it. 5) Prefer APIs already used elsewhere in THIS codebase (grep src/) — consistency with the project beats novelty. 6) If the project ships a component library (shadcn/ui in this stack), use its components instead of hand-rolling. 7) If the API is absent at the installed version, STOP and adapt to what exists — never invent an intermediate version of the library. Cost: seconds per check, versus hours of runtime debugging.

VERIFICATION PLAN (PLANNED — NOT EXECUTED; no evidence exists for v2 claims yet): V1 experimental: demonstrate the full chain on a real installed project — package.json -> lockfile resolved version -> node_modules/<pkg>/package.json version (the sandbox has an installed project; the user workspace only if it has node_modules). V2 experimental (sandbox, TS available): tsc --noEmit flags a call to a nonexistent method on an installed package (negative control) and passes the correct call (positive control). V3 doc-based (NOT yet inspected): lockfile semantics of the project's package manager. The '#1' -> 'recurrent' change REMOVES a claim rather than adding one and needs no evidence — the record now explicitly states the ranking is unquantified.

analyses.comparison: Every prediction matched: the manifest-range/lockfile-pin drift observed on the user's real files; the fabricated package caught at layers 1-2; all four Bun doc statements found verbatim; the sandbox three-layer chain consistent (6.19.2 across lockfile and installed tree); tsc exit codes 0/2/2 with the expected TS2339 and TS2554 error classes.
analyses.alternativeExplanations: (1) Layer 3 could not run on the user's machine (node_modules absent — the workspace was never bun-installed there); the sandbox supplement covers it, clearly labeled as VM-executed. (2) The fabricated-package negative control uses one invented name; catching one plausible fake demonstrates the mechanism, not a statistical guarantee. (3) The docs-describe-latest-release layer is supported by the Prisma docs navigation (v7 exists alongside v6) rather than a dedicated assertion. (4) bun.lock's trailing-comma tolerance required a lenient parse — a strictly-JSON parser would misread the lockfile, which is itself a verification-relevant nuance.
analyses.recommendedModifications: The verified evidence supports the record's revised claims. For the owner's review: the record's step-1 check (package in manifest AND lockfile) is now backed by a real-workspace demonstration including the range-vs-pin distinction; the tsc-vs-grep claim is backed by a controlled sandbox experiment with both failure classes (TS2339 fabricated, TS2554 wrong shape) and the grep blind spot shown. proposedConclusion.summary: Both critical bridge cases passed on real executions on the user's machine: the three-layer verification chain (with layer drift demonstrated and the fabricated dependency caught at manifest+lockfile, node_modules absence honestly recorded), and the Bun lockfile documentation semantics. Supplementary sandbox evidence completes the picture: the installed-tree layer consistent with the lockfile pin, and tsc catching both fabricated APIs and wrong call shapes that grep cannot see. Environmental limitation: node_modules and tsc are not available on the user's machine itself — those layers were verified in the Z.ai sandbox as the record's plan itself anticipated.
